summary: This PR replaces the Greeting screen with a Quiz screen: a scrolling list with a title and 10 cards, each holding a question and a three-state checkbox. It also commits several IDE settings files from the .idea folder. The main problem is that the checkboxes don't do anything: their state is fixed and tapping them is ignored. Two IDE files also contain settings for one person's machine.

accepted.title: The quiz checkboxes can't be checked
accepted.whatGoesWrong: A user taps a checkbox to answer a question, and nothing happens. Every checkbox is always shown as Indeterminate, and its click handler is empty. All 10 cards look the same and none can be answered.
accepted.whyItMatters: The quiz screen's only interactive part doesn't work, so users can't answer anything.
accepted.howToFix: Store a state for each card, for example `val states = remember { mutableStateListOf(*Array(10) { ToggleableState.Off }) }`. Pass `states[index]` to the checkbox and update it in onClick, for example moving from Off to On. Put the state in a ViewModel or use rememberSaveable so answers survive screen rotation.

accepted.title: Committed IDE settings name one developer's JDK
accepted.whatGoesWrong: misc.xml sets the project JDK to `jbr-25`, a JDK name from one developer's machine. deploymentTargetSelector.xml holds per-user device choices. When another developer opens the project, Android Studio may report an invalid JDK or overwrite these files. That leaves the files modified in git all the time.
accepted.whyItMatters: It creates noise and setup friction for every contributor and has nothing to do with the feature.
accepted.howToFix: Remove `.idea/misc.xml` and `.idea/deploymentTargetSelector.xml` from the commit, and add them to `.gitignore` along with the other per-user .idea files already listed there.
